ship.lore:
Although most would morph over their storied lives, each was once famous among Earth’s populace. Supremely tough, adaptable and repairable, each is valued by Resistance admirals, who usually max-out the platform’s armament. Rarely, they survive in their original configuration - finding the lonely, becalmed Edensphere was a revelation to the UCM - a self-sustaining Amazon ecosystem, she is a final testament to Earth’s lost biodiversity. Most Explorers are brutal chop-shop jobs of multiple ships with working modules swapped in for expediency. In their first day’s fighting during the Battle for Earth, the Vega Scrapfleet famously jumped the crippled Santa Maria back to their staging area and had her back in action within 48 hours, looking quite different. The grandest of these dinosaurs are known as Colonisers - among the largest ships ever built by mankind, they exceed modern dreadnoughts in displacement. Once they carried whole populations toward their new lives, now they end them en-mass.

Explorers are battleship-sized beasts, built from more standard modules than Pathfinders. Larger exploration fleets would typically be headed by one.

ship.name: Pathfinder Interstellar Raft
ship.lore:
Unlike most ships, whole sections of superstructure can be swapped out for specialist modules, including weapons, storage, hangars, refineries, factories, cores and even vast bio-domes to seed empty planets with Earth’s fauna and flora. Since every expedition was unique, no two Pathfinders are identical. Today, these ancient vessels perfectly suit the Resistance and are frequently armed beyond their historic configurations. Like most pre-war designs, Kalium still builds Pathfinders, although why they have built quite so many of these fighting exploration ships vexes the UCM’s High Council.

Among mankind’s oldest FTL-capable ships, Pathfinders offer resistance admirals extreme toughness and flexibility in a battlecruiser-sized package. These mighty vessels once boldly plied new space, often commanding smaller exploration fleets on random jump expeditions. Missions lasting years made bulk essential, since aid or resupply was never assured, given the rarity of FTL-capable ships in those heady days. Once humanity broke from their unequal alliance with the Shaltari, alien raids were a frequent problem. Central to the design brief was reparability in the field and mission-specific configuration.

ship.name: Yamamoto Grand Battleship
ship.lore: The Yamamoto is a class of grand battleship designed and constructed by the EAA prior to the arrival of the Scourge. Designed alongside the Nimitz-class, the Yamamoto is one of the last grand battleships built by twinning the hulls of existing battleships. Unlike its sister class, it took an alternate approach to enabling the spinal vent lance, forgoing launch bays in favour of an even more enlarged power core. This allowed the Yamamoto to mount a pair of 9K mass driver turrets as secondary weapons, making it even more deadly when going weapons-free. To fill out the remainder of its power budget, a pair of chin-mounted torpedo launchers were added, giving the class even more ship-killing power. By virtue of its loadout, the Yamamoto proved an exceptional threat against individually tough targets — though its primary weapon's instability means its captain must carefully judge between maximising damage or potentially broiling the engineering team assigned to maintain it.

ship.namesake: Isoroku Yamamoto (1884-1943), the Japanese admiral who conceived and directed the attack on Pearl Harbor.

ship.name: Nimitz Grand Battleship
ship.lore: The Nimitz is a class of grand battleship designed and constructed in the pre-Scourge era, and is one of the last classes built by twinning existing battleship hulls (alongside its sister class, the Yamamoto). While the shipbuilding technique was crude, it offered more flexibility in its modularity versus the newer, purpose-built grand battleship classes. As a result, the class proved the perfect test bed for the spinal vent lance — a risky experiment made cost-viable by its construction method. The vent lance proved to be the largest vent cannon ever built, necessitating a massive hull and extremely high power requirements. Owing to this power draw, the Nimitz mounts NC-16 missile turrets as secondary weapons alongside hangar bays. Despite the extreme hazards of carrying such a large vent cannon, several Nimitz battleships have survived into the modern day, where they are fielded by Resistance fleets, including Kalium — their superlative ship-killing power well worth the trade-off of occasionally cooking entire engineering teams.

ship.lore: The Drake class was the first human vessel to mount an apocalypse-grade, non-nuclear weapon: the Spinal Mass Annihilator. It is an enormous kinetic energy weapon capable of driving a house-sized lump of tungsten carbide coated, ultra-dense metal clean through a battleship, lengthwise. Such a weapon required enlarged power cores aboard the twinned Old Battleships and the new central core to feed it, necessitating the loss of its broadsides. Secondary armaments include NC-16 missile turrets and a pair of heavy vent canons to burst surplus energy onto any survivors.

This surplus and the relative simplicity of its armaments gave the Farragut legendary endurance and has made it a favourite of Resistance fleets. Offering the same quad-turret NC-16 battery and NC-12 broadsides as the Barbarossa, the Farragut also mounts six enormous torpedoes in three tubes, allowing for two devastating spreads. Few ships can survive a single salvo from this ancient leviathan.

Developed alongside the Barbarossa, the Farragut offers a more straightforward weapons loadout with surplus power capacity.

Unlike most vessels with a detector role, the Barbarossa typically fights at the forefront of any engagement, caring little for the increased visibility that comes with running active scanners due to its already vast signature. To fully utilise the remaining power, the class’s lethality was further bolstered by a pair of chin-mounted vent canons.

A specialist variant of the Nelson, the Barbarossa replaces the power-hungry, early mass driver turrets with NC-16 missiles. In addition to offering increased lethality at close range, this frees up power for an enormous scanner array.

ship.name: Nelson Grand Battleship
ship.lore: The Nelson is a class of grand battleship constructed during the pre-Scourge era, and stands as one of the first grand battleship classes built by humanity. After humanity's relationship with the Shaltari soured, the EAA found itself woefully outgunned by the suddenly-hostile alien race. Rather than commit to a costly scrapping process, shipbuilders hastily twinned existing battleship hulls around newer, vastly-improved power cores. These new ships — dubbed "grand battleships" — featured significantly improved scanners, armaments and point defences while offering better survivability. One of the first built this way, the Nelson was created by pairing two Musashi battleships together. The reliability of the overbuilt Musashi hull, coupled with its low-power-draw weapons, made the Nelson a potent and survivable threat against the Shaltari forces of the era. Many have survived to the modern day, employed by independent Resistance crews and Kalium alike.

ship.name: Vanguard Old Battleship
ship.lore: EAAS Vanguard was once the only example of her class. A development of the earlier Iowa, she incorporated vent canon broadsides and what was once a state-of-the-art power core. She proved unstable due to her armament and insufficient cooling and was ultimately lost with all hands over Eden Prime during the Scourge invasion. However, her plans were widely available due to her age, and since then, many foolhardy and/or bloodthirsty resistance admirals have converted Musashis and Lexingtons into Vanguards using more recent cores and custom-built vent canons.
ship.namesake: HMS Vanguard, the last and largest battleship ever built for the Royal Navy, completed just after the Second World War.

ship.name: Iowa Old Battleship
ship.lore: Much rarer than its sister classes, the Iowa was the earliest known testbed of vent cannon technology. It mounts a pair of turreted heavy vent canons by dispensing with any broadside armament, freeing up space for a much enlarged, antique power core. Ventral NC-16 missiles complete the Iowa’s armament, given their negligible power drain. Like all Old Battleships, the Iowa has poor scanners and point defences by modern standards, necessitating careful use.
ship.namesake: USS Iowa (BB-61), lead ship of the US Navy's last class of battleships, famed for her nine 16-inch guns.

ship.name: Lexington Old Battleship
ship.lore: Like other Old Battleships, the Lexington could rightly belong in a museum, although it’s still a formidable warship today. Many survived the Scourge invasion since they were mostly relegated to frontier picket duty, being outmoded even then. In the hard centuries that followed, the Lexington has proven its worth countless times, offering a reliable loadout of NC-16 missiles, a single ventral torpedo, and a fair-sized strike craft hangar. The negligible power drain of all of these gives the class excellent toughness, endurance, and utility for its age.
ship.namesake: USS Lexington, the US aircraft carrier nicknamed 'Lady Lex', lost in the Battle of the Coral Sea in 1942.

ship.name: Musashi Old Battleship
ship.lore: Once among the mightiest ships ever built by mankind, the Musashi is now a relic, even among resistance fleets. Introduced in the mid-24th century, around the time of first contact with the Shaltari, the youngest of these veterans is over 300 years old. However, they were overbuilt for the rigours of exploration and have proven supremely reliable. Its broadsides of chemically fired N-12 cannons are undemanding workhorses with a low power draw, so most Musashi’s spinal turrets have been refitted with 9K mass drivers over the centuries.
ship.namesake: The Japanese battleship Musashi, among the two largest ever built, sunk under a hail of US air attacks in 1944.

ship.lore: The Tribune is heavier, slower and tougher than modern battlecruisers. It shares a superstructure and one mass driver turret with the more common Phalanx class. The remainder of its firepower comes from two conventional cannon turrets and an increased close action capability. However, the Tribune is unusual for a full combat ship of this size in that it features capacity for bulk landers. Its only real modern descendants are the PHR’s assault troopships. In addition though, the Tribune has a significant flight deck, making it a fleet carrier as well. In combination, the Tribune is a jack of all trades, able to adapt to fluid combat situations better than most ships.

ship.lore: The Triumvir has been one of the most valued ships to the Resistance since escaping the Scourge invasion. Shipyards mostly being a lost luxury, any repairs had to be run in the void with the help of other ships - the Triumvir’s specialty. Though a military vessel with fighting armour and battlecruiser tonnage, most of its superstructure is dominated by an insectile bank of extending service armatures. Long-term, Triumvirs can run complex repairs that take weeks. In battle they inject expanding, rapid-cure polymer foam into hull breaches, armour cracks and voided areas, keeping a ship in the fight longer. Despite their value beyond the battlespace, many Resistance admirals gladly risk fielding Triumvirs for the sake of the greater good. To support its activities, the Triumvir has a large internal hangar for various service craft from shuttles to engineering barges. Triumvirs that go to battle tend to replace some of these with regular fighters and bombers to add offensive and escort capability.

ship.lore: The Senator was classified at the time of the Scourge invasion and for good reason. The class was an affront to many EAA government cornerstones. Though records were lost in the invasion, historians believe the Senator was secretly developed by Earth Fleet Command’s shadowy Section Green, without civilian government knowledge. If true the military was preparing contingencies for city-wide insurrections; if not the government was. Some whisper that a military coup was tabled and this was an anti-uprising deterrent, though the Scourge put paid to anyone’s plans. Though comparatively rare then, most Senators survived the invasion since friendly fire on a biblical scale would have resulted if such terrors were used in “defence”. Kalium is rumoured to build these new - disquieting, if unsurprising. The Senator carries three armoured VX nerve agent torpedoes packed with dispersal cluster bomblets. If detonated over a city, any contact with the agent results in spasms, vomiting, paralysis and asphyxiation, leaving infrastructure untouched. As a terror weapon, the Senator carries no significant long range anti-ship firepower, but does include powerful missile turrets for close defence. Combat doctrine stressed the use of the Senator’s then advanced detector array to  warn of enemy vessels, or roving reporters after the scandal of the century.

variants.name: Vicarius
variants.lore:
While the Senator class battlecruiser was an abhorrent and unsanctioned creation of certain paranoid admirals, EAAS Vicarius was downright infamous. She was once the sole example of her class and, it is now understood, instrumental in the Cleansing of Wolfrum. In 2495, twelve years before the Scourge invasion, the mining colony of Wolfrum rebelled, violently. Soon, an unknown vessel of battlecruiser tonnage appeared above the capital and unleashed a spread of VX gas bombardment munitions, slaughtering the entire population.

No comment was made by the military and the government vehemently denied involvement. Senior individuals were executed in the following years, and often for crimes that should have warranted prison sentences. EAAS Vicarius next appeared as a loner in 2674, her decks cold with a sparse skeleton crew. Her senior officers had apparently boarded another human vessel and had not returned. Now, in 2679, new examples of her class have been spotted among Kalium’s sinister vanguard fleets.

ship.namesake: A senator, one of the elder statesmen of the Roman Senate, the council that steered the Republic and Empire.

ship.name: Gladiator Grand Cruiser
ship.lore: The Gladiator was a limited production test-bed for Vent Cannon technology, developed from the Centurion class by Equatorial Yards inc. At the time, it was hoped that they could eventually replace all guns that used physical munitions. However, the number of accidents and dangerous internal meltdowns convinced the EAA to shelve the concept of an all-Vent-Cannon ship such as the Gladiator, since it has no other weapons should the core grow unstable. The Resistance has been able to overlook these flaws, given the advantages the class offers. Without physical munitions, it never needs ammunition resupply so can operate offensively more or less indefinitely, providing its cores are maintained. Also, Vent Cannons are especially devastating, if unreliable. Such power is particularly attractive to Kalium – the rogue Colony has produced fully three times the number of this class than were laid-down before the Scourge invasion.

Designs for Resistance cruisers are widely varied, to the point where listing each variation ever sighted would be as expansive as a list of each individual admiral in the galaxy. As such, it’s best to describe them in general terms, focused more on their capabilities and armaments than form. In this context, a “cruiser” means anything from a Heavy Cruiser to a Light Cruiser, as the UCM would classify them. A further complication is the optional presence of ablative armour panels, adding the classification of “armoured” to the description. Typically, all Resistance cruisers offer respectable survivability, low cost and a broad choice of weaponry. However, their outdated designs do show in poor scan range and limited point defence. Some of these vessels have been adapted from civilian service, generally by adding weapons. Such modified ships often have ablative armour added to overcome their relatively weak designs.

variants.name: Kalium KNC-5
variants.note: KNC-5 counts as Light Cruiser (with NC-16 Missile Bank + 2 Vent Cannon Turrets)
variants.lore:
Generally, Kalium’s ruling Kabal prefers to replicate proven pre-war designs than to innovate, with a focus on numbers. However, after Kalium’s first major blooding in the opening stages of the Battle for Earth, deficiencies became apparent. Visitors to UCM vessels brought back memories (and hushed whispers) that their ships might not be as advanced as their Kabal proclaimed. While combat performance was solid, helped by the iron discipline of their career-sailors, the lack of modern “dressings” in crew areas verged on embarrassing. Clunky 2D viewscreens, general lack of lighting and spartan comforts were more visible than inefficient drives and un-optimised construction.

Kalium’s latest vessels, while essentially the same underneath, have a more modern, distinct appearance as well as countless internal refinements. Kalium still does not favour colourful class names, though. A “KNC-5” (Kalium Navy Cruiser, Type 5) is one of their most common, new line cruisers, armed with a pair of vent cannon turrets and a potent close action missile array.

variants.name: Kalium KNC-12
variants.note: KNC-12 counts as Light Cruiser (with Vent Cannon Turret + 2 Fighters & Bombers)
variants.famousShips: Beton Brut, Chaimberlain Powelbon, Du Hast
variants.lore:
Kalium’s newest vessels’ unique aesthetic suggests a deliberate attempt by the Kabal to “brand” their forces, or at least to make them distinct from the old, tired ships of Resistance fleets. Certainly, the brutalist design speaks of utility, strength and a total disdain for beauty – not that the UCM cares much for those either, but at least they don’t seem to revel in them. The KNC-12 Fleet Carrier is one of the more common, offering excellent, cost-efficient utility to any admiral by way of a potent (if unsafe) vent cannon turret and a double set of launch bays. Unlike the Shaltari, Kalium has no shortage of pilots.

The increasing percentage of these newest vessels in recent engagements speaks of the extreme speed at which the Kabal can build ships – helped, no doubt, by the multitudes under the whip of penal servitude. Their manufacturing capacity is also fearsome, as scattered reports of the class operating under the flag of several Resistance fleets now exist, suggesting that Kalium’s resupply arrangements, as the only manufacturer of old military hardware, have expanded greatly in recent months.

ship.lore: Guy Fawkes (clearly not his real name) is infamous for one thing — blowing battleships to smithereens with massive fire ships. His small, eager crew of plastique-happy privateers are backed by a personal deep-space shipyard kitted out for packing ships with explosives and armouring them enough to survive a one-way charge towards any enemy of any sufficiently flush benefactor. Fawkes prefers old colony ships as candidates, given their cavernous holds. To their creaking frames his engineers affix laughably thick frontal armour plates, having freed up mass by tearing out crew quarters, weapons, spares and anything needed for long-term operations. In combat, Fawkes flies his ship-sized munition personally alongside an insanely loyal — or just insane — skeleton crew. They all jump ship in escape pods at the last possible moment, coordinating with a nearby friendly vessel to collect them so they might do it all again another day. He's currently on Parliament XIII, with no indication he might retire for the quiet life among his explosively gotten gains.
ship.namesake: Guy Fawkes (1570-1606), the conspirator caught beneath Parliament with the gunpowder meant to blow it sky-high in 1605.

ship.lore: The Collins is a class of ship designed to serve as part of humanity's exploration fleets over three hundred years ago. These fleets prized self-sufficiency and endurance above all else — two traits the Collins provided by repairing and refuelling the fleet's shuttles and escorts. Following the Scourge's arrival, the Collins swiftly became an important part of Independent Resistance fleets due to its supply of tough fuel haulers and engineering wings. A single Collins can keep entire squadrons of fighters in the air long after they would otherwise have had to return to their motherships, maintaining the fighter screen for both defensive and scouting purposes.
ship.namesake: Michael Collins (1930-2021), the Apollo 11 command-module pilot who orbited the Moon alone while his crewmates landed.

ship.lore: the first humans to set foot on one of the UCM’s colonies did so from a bulk lander deployed by an Aldrin class colony ship. These hardy ships formed the vanguard of most expeditions and were deployed when a world looked suitable for habitation or exploitation. Bulk landers were preferred to dropships in those halcyon days, since advanced opposition was unlikely and heavy machinery was always needed planetside. Today, the Aldrin offers the capacity of a troopship in a package the size of a destroyer, possible since these ships were never designed for open warfare so offer additional space. Being below cruiser sized, they can also operate in atmosphere, protecting them from void weapons fire. Built to a standard not seen since the exploration days, they can withstand abuse no modern civilian vessel could survive.
ship.namesake: Buzz Aldrin (born 1930), the Apollo 11 lunar-module pilot and the second human to walk on the Moon.

ship.lore: The Armstrong, Aldrin and Collins are some of the earliest human starships still in service; dating back to the late 24th century, they were designed for endurance exploration. Every UCM colony was discovered by hit-and-miss expeditions, requiring many semi-random foldspace jumps until a usable world could be found, explored and given a node. Such dependable hardiness ensured three centuries' service. In size and capability they equal a modern destroyer, though in displacement they are more akin to cruisers due to multiple redundancies, cavernous storage and antique tech. The Armstrong is armed with a deadly HF-6 Clearance Laser which — while useful in the long task of asteroid clearance — is put to much better use against enemy ships, offering Resistance an option for Burnthrough.
ship.namesake: Neil Armstrong (1930-2012), commander of Apollo 11 and the first human to set foot on the Moon, in 1969.

ship.lore: Add a massive engine bank to a set of launch bays and you have the Baleares, a carrier whose strike craft are self-powered. Even today, the Baleares is one of the fastest carriers in mankind’s fleets and embodies the concept of the pre-war pocket carrier. Typically, a carrier will operate beyond line of sight or shielded within the fleet to strike at the enemy’s centre. Since almost nothing can keep pace with the Baleares, it fights quite differently and offers unusual advantages. Baleares captains use their speed to break out from the main fleet, surge forward and launch their daring waves at small, rearguard support vessels. These targets usually offer little point defence, making them vulnerable to strike craft though they are usually beyond their range - not so with the Baleares.
ship.namesake: The Balearic Islands, whose slingers were prized as deadly skirmishers in the armies of Carthage and Rome.

ship.lore: The Sagittarii is essentially an engine bank with a weapons suite attached to the prow. Extraordinarily fast (especially for a Resistance vessel), almost all the ship’s power is consumed by the drives, necessitating a low power primary armament. Fortunately, pre-war designers still used crude, chemical-based guns and they mounted four of the largest in fixed-forward positions. Though much fatter, the N-12 cannon offers destructive parity with modern medium mass rivers. Built in various configurations over the years, the Sagittarii is a typical pre-war cutter, if ‘typical’ can even be applied to such a specialist ship. Cutters were bulkier and actually more common in the EAA Navy than in the modern UCMF, since speed could compensate for inferior scanning technology in first strike missions. Many escaped the Scourge invasion using that speed and have been valued assets to the Resistance ever since. Kalium’s Kabal appreciate the brutal simplicity of the design, so still manufacture them new in state-run yards.
ship.namesake: The sagittarii, the auxiliary archers who lent ranged firepower to the close-packed ranks of the Roman legions.

ship.lore:
This can augment Resistance vessels’ older scanning technology and aid a skilled captain in targeting vulnerable spots on enemy

Galileo orbital telescopes are among the oldest human ships still flying. In the earliest days of foldspace exploration, jumps to un-noded locations had to be conducted in drive-wearing ‘hops’ or random inaccuracy would result. Surveying potential jump locations for potential and celestial threats necessitated a ship built around a gigantic, high-power scanner. Speed was unimportant, so the superstructure of the more common Newton class monitor was chosen as an efficient, low-cost base. Never a military vessel, the Galileo is unarmed besides basic point defence. Surviving Galileos were vital to stranded Resistance fleets forced to use archaic jump-hops to seek the meagre resources not already discovered and either captured by the Scourge or (as with the Colonies) had their node codes changed. Being able to detect enemy activity from a vast distance is also of great use to those small remnant fleets hiding in the cracks of the galaxy - lest they be ambushed. At battlespace level, such observational power can be turned on in-system targets to achieve extraordinary definition unachievable with smaller hardware.
ship.namesake: Galileo Galilei (1564-1642), the Italian astronomer whose telescope revealed Jupiter's moons and remade our view of the heavens.

ship.lore: The Newton was the most common pre-war naval defence monitor in the service of mankind. Unlike modern monitors, the class is visually closer to a space station than a ship, suiting its near- static mission profile. With the speed of the Scourge invasion, few could manoeuvre into a firing position - unfortunate since it packs an enormous mass driver for a frigate-sized vessel. The XN-40 “Godray” was designed to destroy incoming targets long before they could return fire. It sits on a swivel mount, allowing not only tracking of deep space, but precise bombardment of surface targets. Pre-war this was largely used to quell any thoughts of insurrection or to level inhospitable landscape prior to surface exploration. Today, the Newton still brings incredible firepower for its cost, at the price of speed and survivability. This gives it a valued place on the gun line of any Resistance or Kalium admiral capable of harnessing this ship’s strengths. Although unwieldy to bring to a forward position, its bombardment and anti-shipping firepower can lend the class a new lease of life in an offensive role.
ship.namesake: Sir Isaac Newton (1642-1727), who set down the laws of motion and gravitation that govern every ship's course.

ship.lore: As with cruisers, the sheer variety of frigate designs in service with the Resistance is staggering. Similarly, it’s best to discuss them in terms of capability and armament. Many of these ships were originally civilian-grade, but have since had weapons added in response to dire need. All Resistance frigates are faster than cruisers, offering a first strike/ flanking option. They are often used to seek and destroy key enemy vessels early in an engagement, to protect the larger ships in the fleet. Their weapons basically define their role and mode of attack, be that aggressive close-action or standoff fire. In this context, the term “frigate” also encompasses Strike Carriers and unarmed Electronic Warfare Ships. A common pre-war practice was the production of Heavy Frigates, heavily armoured often with two main weapon systems. These have fallen out of favour with the UCMF due to high cost and the drain of dual weapons systems on engine power.

ship.lore: Though lacking in military resources, most fleets scattered by the Scourge invasion had a high proportion of merchantmen - rightly more likely to run than engage. Forced to be inventive, ragtag Resistance groups sought to repurpose civilian vessels to military ends. Haulers often make poor gun platforms but offer capacious internal holds. When combined with ‘repurposed’ shuttles, yachts and small transports, a formidable weapon can result: the Detonator, a hive of remote-operated, explosive-packed fire ships. The most common vessel is a Seneca class - unweildy and utilitarian, it offered pre-war traders the largest storage for the lowest cost, although many other patterns are in service in this unlikely role. Crewing a repurposed flimsy brick fizzing with improvised time bombs is not for the sane and/or skittish. These individuals are treated with wary respect when on shore leave, notable in the bar due to singed hair - if they’ve survived to douse their burns in booze. In the service of Kalium, Detonators are employed in an altogether more sinister, regimented fashion, which says a lot of how much the Kabal values flesh and blood.
ship.namesake: Seneca the Younger (c.4 BC-AD 65), the Roman Stoic philosopher and statesman, tutor to Nero and forced to take his own life.

ship.lore: The Munifex is a fairly typical corvette – fast, atmospheric-capable and designed to kill Strike Carriers, as well as their opposite numbers. It is armed with specialist missiles, much like the UCM’s Santiago class.
ship.namesake: A munifex, the ordinary Roman legionary liable for the full burden of fatigues and labour.

ship.name: Kalium KNC-5 Line Cruiser
ship.lore:
Generally, Kalium's ruling Kabal prefers to replicate proven pre-war designs than to innovate, with a focus on numbers. However, after Kalium's first major blooding in the opening stages of the Battle for Earth, deficiencies became apparent. Visitors to UCM vessels brought back memories (and hushed whispers) that their ships might not be as advanced as their Kabal proclaimed. While combat performance was solid, helped by the iron discipline of their career-sailors, the lack of modern `dressings' in crew areas verged on embarrassing. Clunky 2D viewscreens, general lack of lighting and spartan comforts were more visible than inefficient drives and un-optimised construction.

Kaluim's latest vessels, while essentially the same underneath, have a more modern, distinct appearance as well as countless internal refinements. Kalium still does not favour colourful class names, though. A `KNC-5' (Kalium Navy Cruiser, Type 5) is one of their most common, new line cruisers, armed with a pair of vent cannon turrets and a potent close action missile array.

ship.name: Kalium KNC-12 Line Cruiser
ship.lore:
Kalium's newest vessels' unique aesthetic suggests a deliberate attempt by the Kabal to `brand' their forces, or at least to make them distinct from the old, tired ships of Resistance fleets. Certainly, the brutalist design speaks of utility, strength and a total distain for beauty - not that the UCM cares much for those either, but at least they don't seem to revel in them. The KNC-12 Fleet Carrier is one of the more common, offering excellent, cost-efficient utility to any admiral by way of a potent (if unsafe) vent cannon turret and a double set of launch bays. Unlike the Shaltari, Kalium has no shortage of pilots.

The increasing percentage of these newest vessels in recent engagements speaks of the extreme speed at which the Kabal can build ships - helped, no doubt, by the multitudes under the whip of penal servitude. Their manufacturing capacity is also fearsome, as scattered reports of the class operating under the flag of several Resistance fleets now exist, suggesting that Kalium's resupply arrangements, as the only manufacturer of old military hardware, have expanded greatly in recent months.

A Group gains a single Spike each time it uses its Shield saves (regardless of the number of saves made per use).
Hits caused by Boarding Actions cannot be saved by Shield Saves.

ship.lore:
The UCM first encountered the Pungari as part of a Shaltari force during Phase 2 of the Reconquest. Unlike their masters, they were prolific in numbers. In them, the Shaltari found a subservient race to exploit in much the same way they had planned for humanity.

Sightings of Pungari ships were reported shortly afterwards—not all had fallen in with the Shaltari. Apparently, the Pungari are new to starfaring; their blocky ships are primitive yet robust. Instead of the low-crew, high-firepower approach advanced generators afford to other races, the Pungari leverage sheer numbers. Routinely, they hurl thousands into suicidal boarding actions; something Pungari do willingly and—as far as UCM soldiers can tell—with much glee. Their stocky frames may cope with the extreme g-forces involved, unencumbered by too much brain to damage.

When encountering Pungari it is always a coin toss on whether they attack or not. They may try to broker simple alliances, happy to plunge into the wars of other races without expecting much in return, beyond a master to serve in awe.

ship.lore:
Hyperyacht Aurorum, launched 2493, was commissioned by Caesar Dun, boss of the East Eden Syndicate. She was uniquely built to impeccable standards, riddled with unregistered spaces, and armed far beyond EAA-sanctioned levels. While using her peerless stealth capabilities to evade justice, he unwittingly dodged the Scourge invasion. After months of shadowing a survivor flotilla, Caesar was garrotted by his lieutenant, who took Aurorum to join the refugees.

Today, Aurorum serves as the flagship of Karl Stieglitz, head of the galaxy's most infamous mercenaries: The Decapitators. This privateer flotilla earned dark renown during the Battle of Earth in the vanguard of the Vega Scrapfleet but is now a gun for hire. Stieglitz has already been approached by Kalium and, it is rumoured, the PHR. The UCM has yet to decide how to respond.

ship.lore:
Pre-war System Admirals had unconscionable budgets and could procure ships for their battlefleet with little oversight from Earth. When it came to their personal ship, this created the conditions for a strange offering from the naval yards: opulence. Trident Industrial met this need lavishly with the Palatine Class Command Barge. An unusual ship of battlecruiser tonnage, it shares the typical style on the outside, but inside, no expense was spared. Marble, ebony and craftsmanship are terms you don't hear in military circles. Indeed, a single Palatine cost more than three Grand Battleships to build. The class features twelve overlarge lifeboats of unique design, the Magellan, each closer to an armoured yacht than an escape craft. Even the ship's guns use expensive, low-observable shells to reduce the ship's signature in combat. To offset this fabulous cost, Trident Industrial offered vessels to the private sector; owners included planetary governors, corporate titans and infamous syndicate heads.

Though rare, a high proportion survived the Scourge invasion and the hard centuries that followed due to quality, their excessive point defences, and the fact that owners weren't generally the sorts to go down fighting. Since everything on the Palatine was overbuilt to the highest standards, survivors are still prized, capable ships. Their bygone splendour and the hand-ground perfection of their optics even make them worthwhile to the Republic's Grand Fleet, which operates several, mostly the former property of prophesy-spooked CEOs. Kalium possesses two which the UCM is aware of, although apparently their more opulent spaces have been painted grey—they're still Shangrilanian inlay underneath. The UCM has five on their lists, including River Queen, which is reserved for Presidential use. Such ships could be built today, but the cost would make no military sense—it never did.
ship.namesake: The Palatine, the Roman hill at the heart of the city where the emperors raised their palaces - the root of the word itself.

ship.lore: The Centurion was the most common standardised vessel of cruiser tonnage in the pre-war EAA Terran Grand Fleet. In those days the definition of Cruiser was somewhat broader; today, such a bulky vessel is designated as a Grand Cruiser, a classification not really in use with the UCMF. In bulk (though not in firepower), it is more akin to a modern Heavy Cruiser. It has truly excellent ceramic armour plating that outclasses all but defence monitors in the modern UCMF. The Centurion also features many of the typical advantages and disadvantages of vintage naval architecture. Originally manufactured by Trident Industrial over Olympus Prime, the design was soon licensed to Earth-based Equatorial Yards Inc. Only the licensed Earth pattern is still built today, by Kalium, though it also operates legacy Olympus Centurions. Its simple but effective all-gun primary armament provides an excellent blend of destructive power and reliability. The class requires low weapon maintenance - a welcome factor that certainly isn’t the case with some of the more esoteric and experimental armaments in mankind’s pre-war arsenal. Its primary armament is broadsides of transition mass drivers, alongside an oversized twin pure mass driver turret, more in keeping with modern UCMF gunnery, albeit with much heavier projectiles.

ship.lore:
The Hyperyacht Somniferum is not a sight civilized governments want to see on situation reports. Colloquially known as "the party bus", a spike in crime and illegal substances usually follows in its wake. Somniferum's current owner is the "Master of Ceremonies" Maeby Hy. The Somniferum is almost unrecognisable from its initial configuration as an Eden Aerospace Systems Luxury Liner. Lab explosions, combat damage, and ad-hoc refits have all added to it's hodge-podge appearance.

One of these many changes to the ship is the addition of a peculiar weapon system. While it has no official name, the crew and any who face it have dubbed it "Party Poppers". This weapon system fires armour piercing fragmenting flechettes that disperse airborne narcotics and electromagnetic interference into its target. Far too small and numerous to effectively track, this weapon is able to bypass the majority of a ship's point defences and deliver strikes straight to the hull.

The Somniferum is rarely seen over combat zones, preferring to stick to those planets that are safe enough for civilian travel. While able to defend itself against small time competitors, the ship isn't built for combat. More often than not, the Somniferum will make a hasty exit from a planet as soon as it detects any law enforcement on an intercept course.

ship.name: LKS Dredger

specialRules.name: Industrial Design
specialRules.description: Improve this Group’s Backup save by 2 when rolling to save hits due to Debris Fields.

ship.lore:
A relentless machine of industry, built to mulch, sift, and extract until its timer runs dry. It drills deep, rips apart rock, and spits out raw profit, indifferent to the hands that keep it running. No legacy, no ownership, just a contract ticking toward expiration. When time is up, it moves on, leaving its crew behind, waiting for the next company to stake its claim on the battered frame. Inside, the workers endure the constant grind, wedged between failing systems and the unyielding demand for productivity. Comfort is non-existent, maintenance is endless.

Equipped with a heavy duty drill and front mounted mining array, this vessel doesn't just extract minerals, it carves deep trenches into asteroid surfaces and space debris, kicking up clouds of pulverized rock and metallic sediment. A network of sediment filters and gravity sifting tanks separates valuable ore from dust before storing the processed materials in its cargo bays.

Prominently displayed on the ship's exterior, the countdown display isn't a warning, it's a fact. The contract will expire, and if it doesn't get topped up, the vessel moves on to whatever comes next. Passed from one mining company to the next, these hand me down workhorses run until their rental contracts dry up. Refurbished just enough to stay functional, they degrade with every transfer, patched, battered, barely space worthy, considered scrap with engines.

Upper management doesn't care about the ship, only the ore it pulls in before time runs out. The crew works under relentless pressure, knowing there's no guarantee of renewal.

When the timer hits zero, it's out of their hands. Either the contract gets extended, or the ship moves on.

Despite its size, the colossal vessel remains a world of tight corridors for its 190 crew members. Dust and grime clings to every surface, settling in forgotten corners and coating equipment in a fine greasy layer. Minimal comforts, constant maintenance, and the daily expectation that something will break.

ship.name: SLM-9 Resupply Hauler

ship.lore:
A relic from the now liquidated Eden Void Logistics inc, the SLM-9 is a battle tested bulk logistics vessel, trusted for fleet replenishment in high risk environments. Though the company behind its design has since shuttered, the SLM-9 endures as a testament to their engineering prowess and affordability. Its metal cargo frame, hydraulic deployment arms and universal clamps ensure rapid, adaptable resupply of ordnance, fuel, and supplies anywhere. Rugged and inexpensive, the SLM-9 remains a reasonable choice for fleets needing a dependable workhorse at a fraction of the cost of newer models.

Unlike conventional Logistics Vessels that unload cargo gradually, the SLM-9 releases its entire payload in a single, controlled operation. Hydraulic deployment arms manoeuvre the entire cargo bed outward, allowing for structured and efficient transfer without manual unloading.

Built for adaptability, the SLM-9's pincer like grappling arms latch onto ships regardless of docking compatibility. Variable force actuators fine tune pressure, securing a stable hold without compromising hull integrity. Whether resupplying warships or assisting stranded vessels, its clamps ensure critical cargo transfer under any conditions.

The SLM-9's hydraulic deployment arms are its defining feature, but also its greatest liability. If compromised by enemy fire or mechanical failure, the vessel loses its ability to unload cargo entirely, rendering it useless. A damaged deployment system means supplies remain trapped onboard, preventing fleet resupply and turning the ship into dead weight. While reinforced plating offers some protection, direct hits can buckle the arms, leading to catastrophic failure.

Due to its critical vulnerability, the SLM-9 has begun to be phased out in favour of newer resupply haulers with reinforced unloading mechanisms and modular backup systems. The remaining SLM-9 units are considered outdated relics, still operational but increasingly rare.

ship.lore:
The T-Type was once a common sight across many shipyards. Due to the size of many pre-war ships, a way of moving these gargantuan vessels out of drydock was needed. T-Types were devised to be the answer to this sizeable problem. The first batch of these floated out of the assembly lines prior to the first Pathfinder, ready and waiting to guide it to a safe launching point. Since then, countless multitudes of these ships have been constructed. Most serve their entire service life in the void, however some are refitted as lunar landers once their superstructure becomes unusable for its intended purpose.

Only a small amount of these were refit with foldspace drives, the majority were only designed to work around a single planet and its satellites. Those that were refit tend to be found in independent fleets, where they assist in swapping components on their larger vessels. T-Types are not built for any form of combat, though their internal bracing gives them a certain resilience, they are unable to weather any attack from dedicated combat ships.

Some T-Types have been converted to function similarly to mines, albeit with a much more personal weapon system. These have weaponised their towing ability, captains with a death wish will attach their tug to an enemy vessel and set their engines to full. When performed right, this can violently tear vessels in half, though at the cost of the tugboat and its crew.

ship.lore:
The DH-Type represents one of the Colonial Fleet's largest run of dedicated long-range prison ships, built around a standardized architecture of reinforced armour, multi-tier detention decks and automated security. Originally intended strictly for high-risk inmate transport and remote incarceration, wartime pressures pushed the class into broader operational roles.

Though designed with consistent core systems, such as compartmentalized containment blocks, automated defensive suites, ECM shielding, and a C.A.G.E emitter field. The ships grew increasingly variable due to differing missions, retrofits, and partial deactivations. Although uncommon, Individual DH-Type vessels gained their own notoriety, such as Iron Veil, Remnant Forge, Dreadhold and Bright Spire. The DH-Type ships illustrated the evolution through conversions into troop transports, logistics carriers, medical ships, and frontier support platforms, often retaining traces of their original penal infrastructure.

In modern service, L1-class hulls endure as adaptable, if austere, multi-role assets. Their durable construction, intimidating infrastructure, and legacy security systems continue to define their operational character, reflecting both the robustness of the original design and the fleet's ongoing need to repurpose coercive architecture for broader demands.

ship.lore:
The Jah'tar are an independent, if diminished, starfaring race that sails from the planet Jaheria. Over two century's peaceable trade with the UCM's colony of Platina, they have shared some of their history.

Their Time of Many Worlds ended roughly three millennia ago when the Great Adversary came. The Jah'tar do not know if any of their other planets survived. Their lifespans of roughly 35 years make this race-memory dimmer than one might expect, but parallels to mankind's own experience was clear—the Scourge were the likely culprits. Surviving artworks show cruder invading ships, but some Jah'tar technology bears limited similarity to Scourge, and most scientists believe it was absorbed and evolved by the enemy. Jah'tar ships also appear grown rather than made, although theirs are largely pseudo-organic chitin over a fine titanium weave.

The Jah'tar no longer fully understand their own technology. Possibly such knowledge was confined to their lost central worlds, but as in antiquity, all Jah'tar works radiate a passion for style and beauty. They covet precious materials and gems, driving their trade with Platina. In return, the UCM gains access to the Jaherian System's ores and wealth of rare elements essential for FTL drive core construction.

The Jah'tar are rangier than humans with stronger limbs and thick, leathery skin. Naturally placid and artistic, they move in an unhurried way but are fast when pressed. With long, prehensile tails they are agile climbers, leading to some exotic spaces aboard their ships. Their four, quad-jointed digits are equally dextrous on hands or feet, and are in constant motion, possibly as a base layer of communication. Their language is a series of rapid clicks and screeches, so they use human speech in negotiations out of respect for our limited vocal range.

Most of humanity's contact with the Jah'tar is via their famous Startraders—graceful, cruiser-sized ships with lavishly decorated meeting spaces, living areas, and cavernous holds. These vessels are permitted free passage within the Platina System but are closely monitored whenever they appear elsewhere in UCM space, despite being unarmed. Hawkish colonial admirals insist that all that internal space could be put to more nefarious uses. Some Startraders serve as mercenaries with other races in exchange for favourable trades, although the UCM occasionally utilises their services so too. Their value lies with their unique support technologies since the Jah'tar refuse to license any true warships to other's violence.

Relations with the alien Jah'tar is an aberration for the UCM, but these arrangements go back before the Scourge invasion and are frankly easier than conquest. Although Jaheria would inevitably be crushed, Jah'tar weaponry is formidable when they are forced to use it, and high casualties that humanity can ill-afford would result.

ship.lore:
M-Type Barges are the larger cousin of the L-Type. Produced at the same Tharsis Manufacturing shipyards over Mars, the M-Type was designed for corporate bulk shipping. Many and more of these were owned and operated by the enduring shipping companies of old Earth, each of them emblazoned with corporate livery. Designed and built after the L-Type, these ships feature much improved Foldspace drives as well as the latest innovations in structural bracing. Optimisations in production brought the build time on these freight behemoths down to only twice that of the L-Type.

Many of these were spared the events of the Scourge invasion, most would have been slowly moving between the colonies and the cradle worlds, far enough away to make emergency jumps to safety. The initial trade and logistics network of the UCM was built upon the backs of the M-Type, their reliability and availability gave the colonies enough trade stability to recover from the loss of the cradle worlds. M-Types are surprisingly rare in Resistance fleets, most of the captains of these ships were more interested in meeting deadlines and quotas than in doomsday predictions prior to the battle of Vega. Kalium is yet to be seen operating these ships, preferring the L-Type for combat resupply, though may potentially be using M-Types in more secure Kalium controlled systems.

Recent developments in prefabricated defensive structures have allowed a small number of these ships to carry deployable missile defence outposts in place of their normal cargo compliment. These outposts are designed to grant a foothold on a planet and supplement its missile halo while more permanent structures are built, re-purposed, or captured.

ship.lore: The Oblivion OBV64 Barge is a heavily armoured civilian vessel designed to transport extremely hazardous materials, unstable technology, failed reactors, and biohazards, too dangerous to store on planets. These ships travel discreetly between remote depots, derelict battlefields, and disposal zones. Crewed by an extensive team of highly trained specialists under strict quarantine and secrecy protocols, The Oblivion barge handles cargo that is often poorly understood or classified. Their role is to quietly remove dangerous discoveries and remnants from circulation before they can threaten the wider fleet, or attract unwanted attention.

ship.lore:
The Type-87 Terminus Harvester is a colossal reclamation vessel built to consume the unrepairable wreckage of war. Its monolithic maw engulfs chunks up to frigate tonnage, feeding them into vast crushing chambers where superheated hydraulic presses obliterate hull plating to slag. Two VX-22 Flensers detach from its hull, peeling derelicts apart and hauling scraps to their final destruction. Ancient, slow-moving, and relentless, it labours, stripping vessels down to raw material. Within its corroded halls, life is harsh. Dim corridors reek of burning metal as air filters struggle against decades of industrial smog.

The Type-87's wedge-like prow is battered and scarred, worn from decades of grinding through wreckage. Deep gouges and warped plating mark where debris crumpled beneath its relentless push, clearing the way for the behemoth behind.

A monolithic opening capable of engulfing entire frigates, feeding them into a crushing chamber spanning the volume of a megastructure. Inside, reinforced walls lined with titanic hydraulic presses grind vessels down in a superheated maelstrom of pulverized metal, reducing all to molten slag.

Equipped with two VX-22 Flensers, these small salvage vessels dock onto the Harvester's hull when idle but detach to roam wreckage fields. They Brutally peel derelicts apart piecemeal while hauling fragmented components to the crushing maw. Though technically separate, they operate as an extension of the Harvester, ensuring no usable scrap escapes consumption.

When building your fleet, you may choose as many Payload Ships as you like— tonnage limits do not apply to these Ships, and they have no Group size. All Payload S/L Ships must be assigned to a Porter S/L Ship with the same letter. Payload Ships may not activate or be targeted until detached.
Payload Ships take up X of a Porter Ship’s capacity.
During the Porter Ship’s activation, if it is on an Order that allows it to Launch, you may detach one or more of its Payload Ships and place them within 3” of it. In the round they are detached, these Payloads activate together immediately as part of the Porter Ship’s activation after it has completed its Order. In subsequent rounds, all your Payload Ships count as being part of a single Group. Crippling Effects, Spikes, and other rules that affect an entire Group only affect the targeted Payload Ship.
Payload Ships always follow General Quarters Orders, even if its Porter is on different Orders. Payload Ships ignore Coherency rules (and do not gain Formation Benefits), have no Lead Ship, are targeted by attacks individually, and these attacks can only damage the targeted Payload Ship.
If a Payload Ship is attached to a Porter Ship when that Ship is destroyed, the Payload Ship is destroyed.

ship.lore:
The VX-22 Flensers are compact salvage vessels designed for brutal ship dismantling. Their prow mounted sawblades don't cut cleanly, they tear, shred, and rip through wreckage with unrestrained violence. Designed for aggressive reclamation, they are the smaller, more aggressive sibling to the T-Type Tugboat. Where the Tugboat manoeuvres and stabilizes wreckage for controlled processing, the Flensers gut derelicts with reckless brutality, prioritizing destruction over precision.

Heavy rotating saws brutally cut through hull plating, breaking it into manageable pieces and scattering debris as they progress. Instead of delicate incision, the Flensers' sawblades operate at maximum torque, chewing through reinforced bulkheads with enough force to buckle surrounding structure.

Their cutting mechanisms frequently overheat, causing violent energy surges that make their hulls shudder mid operation.

The Flenser hurls debris into the Type-87 Terminus Harvester's compactor bay, sometimes suffering brutal kickback as the churning machinery spits chunks back out. When it happens, the debris slams into its failing frame, worsening the damage and making every load a gamble.

Positioned below the cockpit, this reinforced plating shields pilots from wreckage kicked up during cutting operations. Sloped for maximum deflection, it redirects debris that could slam into the hull with deadly force, absorbing impacts before they buckle metal or breach compartments.

ship.name: PRK-91 Provenance Ark
ship.lore:
A monolithic vessel of unimaginable scale, the Provenance Ark dwarfs most ships. A precursor to the modular construction found on Coloniser class vessels, these ships were a talisman of hope and expansionism. These are the first major terraforming vessels built by mankind, reaching out into an unknown universe. Built to prepare entire worlds for habitation, it carries vast stores of genetic material, atmospheric stabilizers, and autonomous resource systems. The Ark monitors planetary progress through an extensive network of sensors and automated regulators, adjusting atmospheric composition, maintaining microbial balance, and even modulating gravitational and magnetic fields to stabilize emerging terrains.

Entire cities once mere schematics, rise, with power grids, transport arteries, and habitation modules ready long before the first settlers arrive. Inside, Construction drones and biotic cultivators orchestrate the birth of forests, oceans, and breathable atmospheres with the precision of a master artisan.

Many ships of this class feature underslung terraforming torpedo launchers. While near useless in ship to ship combat, these torpedoes are geared towards atmospheric re-entry and contain a plethora of mutagens and nerve agents, some of which would be used on Senator class battlecruisers. Under normal circumstances the use of these would constitute a war crime. Here they are simply used to rid prospective landing areas of their megafauna, causing mass hysteria and aggression in local fauna. Any issues with unruly creatures take care of themselves, and those left over can be cut down by specialised anti-fauna vehicles. Once the LZ is cleared of hostiles, the terraformer can then deploy more traditional terraforming methods.
